llc-meeting-minutes-template.8: Many solo owners sign one annual consent covering the year's major decisions, plus separate consents for big one-off actions.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.12: Which decisions need a member vote? Your operating agreement says. Record those as member resolutions even if managers proposed them.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.15: Store LLC minutes with your other company records (the articles of organization, operating agreement, member list and tax filings), ideally as signed PDFs in a dedicated folder, physical or digital. Some states require LLCs to keep certain records at their principal office, so check your state's rules.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.20: Hold at least one annual meeting and record it, plus log major decisions as they happen. Follow any schedule in your operating agreement. Single-member LLCs can sign one annual written consent for the year's major decisions, with separate ones for big one-off actions.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.21: Usually it is a written consent signed by the sole member, listing resolutions for the year or for a specific decision. That document captures the decision just as minutes would. Banks often ask to see it before opening an account or approving credit.
llc-meeting-minutes-template.24: Yes, in most cases. Signed PDFs stored securely with your other company records work well; just check any record-keeping rules in your state and operating agreement. Hold on to minutes for the life of the company, since they cost nothing to store and can matter years later during a sale, audit or dispute.
